searchText: do you take branches? I can quickly increase the limits for besu and you could try with that? As you said it's pretty straightfoward one note though, one will have to increase the tx gas limit to allow for larger code sizes, I think the 16Mgas limit will have to double too which kind of defeats the tx parallelization bounds we have put in place in EIP-7825 no? what does this have to do with tx gas limit? there is no new gas model if it is save to bump you increase the initcode one can run, you are paying for more gas overshooting the tx limit no? still in range 65,536 × 200 = 13.1 million gas then no one will be able deploy contracts on the new limit that you set it's still in range i am pretty sure. some combinations might fail no wait hmm I need to get back on that to confirm but I bumped into that while running a smoke test here to validate my changes its barely in range this is what claude gave me prob an actual test would be worthwhile to verify but this should be barely in range what about the cost of executing the initcode instructions themselves? is it accounting for that? I think if we went there, it would probably fail today as well. i think it is acceptable to have some combinations failing you can create a computation while(1) loop today in initcode that would fail true worst case tx is O(infinity) i think this is fine. you can maybe lift it in the future if people complain it's a theoretical limit no its the actual limit practically it costs whatever you want it to cost anyways, i think good start nonetheless but I appreciate the point of view. did not think of it just to be clear what I meant with theoretical limit is that I'm not sure if such a tight gap covers most initialization code required for larger contracts. But I guess increasing the limit is already a good improvement for devs
